players.product: RF plasma power generators and matching networks for etch / deposition tools

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl / CFO Christian Witt: H1 2026 net sales rose 5.6% to CHF 239.8 million (12.7% in constant currency), with net sales growth accelerating to 25.7% in the second quarter; PCT and IXM each grew about 15% in constant currency (PCT +6.9% and IXM +10.6% in CHF), while IXS was broadly stable in CHF (+6.9% in constant currency) as CA20 sales offset lower legacy-system sales.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 net sales CHF 239.8 million, +5.6% (+12.7% constant currency); Q2 growth 25.7%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Christian Witt: H1 2026 gross margin returned above 40%; EBITDA grew 36.5% to a 13.1% margin (10.1% in H1 2025); without CHF 4.5 million of one-off costs for the efficiency program and the Penang move, EBITDA would have been CHF 35.9 million (+56.1%) at a 15% margin; net profit rose 33.4% to CHF 13.5 million; H1 ROCE was 8.7% against a cost of capital of roughly 9%, and Comet expects to exceed its cost of capital for FY2026.
quarterly_data.figure: EBITDA margin 13.1%; net profit CHF 13.5 million (+33.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl: FY2026 guidance - net sales of CHF 540 million-CHF 570 million and an EBITDA margin of 14%-17% including one-off items of approximately three percentage points (17%-20% excluding them); CFO Christian Witt: one-off costs of around CHF 15 million-CHF 18 million for the year, most of them in H2 2026; FY2026 capex clearly above 7% but clearly below 10% of sales, normalizing to about 4%-7% of sales once Penang is fully operational; free cash flow and the net debt position are expected to reverse in H2 2026, with a return to strong free cash flow in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales CHF 540 million-CHF 570 million; EBITDA margin 14%-17%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl: the H1 2026 book-to-bill ratio was 1.48, up from 1.36 at the end of Q1 2026, with record orders in PCT; CFO Christian Witt: H1 included stockpile orders, some orders already extend into 2027 (PCT customers placing one-year orders), and Comet expects continued strong order flow in H2 with a lower book-to-bill than in H1 as deliveries rise; customers have increased consignment inventory bin sizes and are drawing on it.

CEO Stephan Haferl: the new Penang manufacturing facility is complete (CHF 19.3 million cash outflow in H1), with production ramp-up and product qualifications in H2 2026 (vacuum-capacitor output growing incrementally this year and accelerating through 2027); with the build-out it is completing in Penang, Comet has capacity till 2028 comfortably above an output of CHF 1 billion per year; there are no serious choke points in its own supply chain, unlike 2021-2022.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity above CHF 1 billion output per year through 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl: the IXS division more than doubled CA20 purchase orders versus year-end 2025 and has received in excess of 10 orders for the CA20 X-ray system for semiconductor defect recognition, including repeat orders from customers using it as a tool of record; CA20 lead times run from about three to four months for simple applications to above six months with qualification; CFO Christian Witt: IXS remains EBITDA negative, will keep double-digit million investments in 2027, and expects CA20 EBITDA break-even latest in FY2028.
quarterly_data.figure: CA20 orders in excess of 10; CA20 EBITDA break-even latest FY2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl: the Synertia RF generator and matchbox platform is gaining customer engagement, with orders now coming from a growing spectrum of customers, also geographically; Comet has adapted prices across its full product spectrum since the beginning of 2026 under value-based pricing and will continue to do so; the efficiency program is on track to finish by end-2027 for a sustainable EBITDA improvement of CHF 20 million-CHF 30 million per year from 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: efficiency program CHF 20 million-CHF 30 million EBITDA improvement per year from 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Stephan Haferl: semiconductor demand is driven by AI infrastructure, advanced packaging and leading-edge technologies; H1 growth was most likely mostly DRAM and logic, NAND capex recovery is starting (mainly for data centers) and he expects NAND orders to keep growing; citing industry forecasts, WFE capex is expected to grow between 17% and 27% in 2026; Comet still assumes a cycle peak around mid-2028, as communicated at its capital market day.
quarterly_data.figure: WFE capex +17% to 27% in 2026 (industry forecasts cited by the CEO)
